papers.title: Climate change drives northward range shifts in invasive forest pests and pathogens
papers.authors: Haoran Wu, Gu Jiqi, Chengzhang Zheng, Yadvinder Singh Malhi, Cecilia A. L. Dahlsjö
papers.abstract: Invasive tree pests and pathogens are increasingly threatening forests worldwide. Understanding how a warming climate and changing precipitation patterns will affect the future distribution ranges of these pathogenic species requires systematic analysis across a variety of host trees and pathogenic species. We analysed 31 major tree pests and pathogens that have caused widespread and extensive damage globally, predicting their current and future distribution under various climate change scenarios using species distribution modelling. Our results showed that tree pests and pathogens will consistently shift northward, threatening northern temperate and boreal forests between the years 2041 and 2080. On the other hand, some warmer regions, including southern Europe, were expected to experience fewer pest and pathogen outbreaks in the future. Annual mean temperature, mean temperature of the warmest quarter, precipitation of the warmest quarter, and precipitation of the driest month contributed to the species distribution models, indicating that warming temperatures and moderate precipitation may promote the survival, reproduction, and spread of the pathogenic agents. papers.title: Current and Future Environmental Suitability of the Nile Grass Rat (Arvicanthis niloticus) in Egypt under CMIP6 Climate Change Scenarios
papers.authors: Maha Mostafa, Mustafa M. Soliman
papers.abstract: Abstract The Nile grass rat ( Arvicanthis niloticus Desmarest, 1822) is one of the most destructive agricultural rodent pests and a primary reservoir host for multiple zoonotic pathogens in Egypt, including Schistosoma mansoni, Fasciola spp., Hymenolepis nana, murine typhus, and plague (Yersinia pestis via Xenopsylla cheopis fleas). Quantifying how ongoing climate change will alter its potential geographic distribution is essential for national rodent control strategies and vector-borne disease surveillance. In this study, we calibrated an optimized Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt version 3.4.4) ecological niche model to determine the contemporary macroclimatic suitability envelope of A. niloticus across Egypt and projected its potential range shifts for the 2050s (2040–2060) and 2070s (2060–2080) under Phase 6 of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project (CMIP6) Shared Socioeconomic Pathways (SSP2-4.5, moderate-emission; SSP5-8.5, high-emission). papers.title: A UAV-based real-time detection system of flowering nectar plants using a lightweight deep learning model
papers.authors: Mingzhu Du, Joao Ricardo Pereira Valente, Coby van Dooremalen, Cao Zhen, Jiwen Huang
papers.abstract: Abstract Purpose Timely knowledge of flowering status and peak blooming periods in transferred areas is crucial for migratory beekeepers to make informed management decisions. Traditional manual field surveys are labor-intensive, time-consuming, and unsuitable for frequent monitoring. Current monitoring approaches using Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAV) rely on offline processing and require complex data analysis by specialists, making them impractical for beekeepers to implement in apicultural settings. Given the short time window for capturing flowering events, especially for species with short florescence periods, an accurate, fast monitoring solution is needed. We developed a UAV-based real-time investigation prototype leveraging edge-intelligence computing for nectar flower detection of Rhus chinensis in complex mountainous field conditions. Methods An improved, high-precision, and lightweight deep learning model based on YOLOv5s was proposed. The model was optimized with acceleration strategies during deployment to reduce inference time. papers.title: Rapid estimation of insect biodiversity using AI assisted image analysis: a cost-effective tool for monitoring and ecological assessmen
papers.authors: Liraz Cabra-Leykin, Tamar Keasar, Chen Keasar
papers.abstract: Protection of natural areas and environmentally friendly management of anthropogenic landscapes require reliable tools for monitoring and comparing biodiversity. Bioindicator-based approaches can support large-scale ecological assessment, but insect monitoring remains constrained by the taxonomic expertise required for species identification. Here, we propose an AI-supported index for estimating the biodiversity of flying insects, based on the diversity of visual features of insect bodies. Flying insects were captured using yellow sticky traps across agricultural and natural habitats, seasons, crops, and sites in Israel's Mediterranean region. Traps were scanned at high resolution and uploaded to a dedicated image database. A machine learning model was used to detect and delineate insects, after which engineered visual features representing body size, color, and shape were extracted. Biodiversity was estimated from distances among feature vectors and compared with taxonomic diversity derived from expert identification of a representative validation set. papers.title: Governing structures in functional areas of Bulgarian farms
papers.authors: Hrabrin BACHEV
papers.source: OpenAlex / Journal of Agriculture, Food and Sustainable Development
papers.abstract: The study of governance structures and contractual modes in agriculture is central to agricultural economics due to their role in coordinating relations, distributing risks, and minimizing costs. In Bulgaria, existing research on agrarian governance remains episodic, reliant on official statistics, and limited to isolated contract types or unrepresentative case studies. To address this gap, this study applies the framework of New Institutional Economics (NIE) to conduct a comprehensive analysis of the structure, governing modes, and evolution of resource supply, services, innovation, risk management, and marketing within Bulgarian farms. Based on a representative survey of 345 commercial farm managers conducted between November 2023 and January 2024, the paper examines how transaction characteristics (asset specificity, uncertainty, frequency) and institutional environment influence farmers' managerial choices across market, contractual, internal, and hybrid modes. The findings demonstrate that NIE methodology effectively captures the complex reality of agrarian transaction governance beyond traditional neoclassical models. papers.title: Identification and power relations of stakeholders in the private forest sector in Poland
papers.authors: Emilia Wysocka-Fijorek, Szymon Żygadło
papers.abstract: This article analyses the private forest sector in Poland, which encompasses over 1.78 million ha (19.3% of the country's forest area) and belongs to approximately 1.7 million owners. The research aimed to identify key stakeholders, examine the dynamics of power relations, and recognise structural, legal, and social barriers to effective forest management. The research methodology combined a narrative literature review with empirical field studies utilising the snowball sampling technique to map informal actor networks, followed by a quantitative survey among 139 key stakeholders and a 100-point constant-sum allocation method to evaluate ecosystem service priorities. In the results, an asymmetry of priorities was diagnosed: public administration focuses on supervisory functions, while owners prioritise pest protection and forest tending. An association paradox was demonstrated – despite a high declarative readiness for cooperation (approx. 89%), the actual level of organisation within associations remains marginal. papers.title: Prevention of Destructive Fishing in the Waters of Tual City: Effective Surveillance and Law Enforcement Strategies
papers.authors: Suharta ., Sigit Bintoro, Riyan Maulana, Ismi Isti Anah
papers.source: Crossref / International Journal of Multidisciplinary Research and Growth Evaluation
papers.abstract: <jats:p>Destructive fishing in the waters of Tual City remains a significant environmental and socio-economic issue, threatening marine biodiversity and the livelihoods of local fishermen. This study analyzes the problem using a SWOT approach, identifying strengths such as existing government regulations and rich marine resources, weaknesses including limited enforcement capacity and economic dependence on harmful fishing practices, opportunities such as growing global demand for sustainable seafood, and threats like illegal fishing and climate change. Based on the SWOT analysis, several policy recommendations are proposed, including strengthening law enforcement, promoting sustainable alternative livelihoods, enhancing education and awareness programs, expanding marine protected areas (MPAs), and creating market incentives for responsible fisheries. These strategies aim to transition Tual City towards sustainable fisheries management, balancing environmental conservation with economic development. Effective implementation of these policies will not only mitigate destructive fishing but also ensure long-term resilience for both the ecosystem and local fishing communities.</jats:p>

papers.abstract: The brown stink bug, Halyomorpha halys (Stål, 1855) (Hemiptera: Pentatomidae), has emerged in recent years as an invasive pest species causing significant economic losses in Türkiye, particularly in hazelnut-growing areas. The pest’s broad host range, high reproductive capacity, and ability to spread rapidly over large areas make the development of sustainable control methods imperative. In this study, the capture efficacy of two different commercial pheromones (100 mg Murgantiol + 80 mg Methyl-E,E,Z-2,4,6–decatrienoate (A) and Cellulose dual-dispenser (B)) in funnel-type traps was compared in a hazelnut orchard located in the Çarşamba district of Samsun Province. The study was conducted between August 28 and 7 November 2025. A total of ten traps were used—five for each pheromone—and the adult individuals caught in the traps were counted and recorded on a weekly basis. The findings revealed that both pheromones were able to attract the pest, but that pheromone “A” demonstrated significantly higher capture performance than pheromone “B” throughout the entire observation period. papers.title: H9N2 avian influenza virus in Bangladesh: three genetically distinct co-circulating subgroups retain a largely conserved antigenic phenotype
papers.authors: Rebecca Daines, Jean-Rémy Sadeyen, Mahmudul Hasan, Tridip Das, Rashed Mahmud Sizer
papers.abstract: Low pathogenic avian influenza (LPAI) H9N2 viruses are endemic in poultry across Bangladesh, causing substantial economic losses and posing a persistent zoonotic risk. Although genetic surveillance has documented ongoing viral evolution, the relationship between genetic diversification and antigenic change remains poorly understood. This study investigated the genetic diversity, reassortment, and antigenic characteristics of contemporary H9N2 viruses circulating in Bangladesh. Phylogenetic analysis of 219 sampled sequences revealed three genetically distinct monophyletic haemagglutinin (HA) G-lineage sub-groups, each characterised by unique amino acid substitutions. In contrast, neuraminidase (NA) displayed similar genetic diversity without distinct phylogenetic clusters. A dual-metric analysis of paired HA and NA phylogenies identified 20 putative reassortant H9N2 viruses. papers.title: Beneath the surface: a survey evaluating ASF preparedness across the Caribbean and Latin America
papers.authors: Rachael Schulte, Michelle L. Schultze, Guillermo Arcega Castillo, Luis Pablo Hervé-Claude, Emilio Arnaldo León
papers.abstract: African swine fever (ASF) threatens pig production across the Americas, yet empirical data on preparedness capacity remain sparse. To inform regional planning and capacity building, we conducted a comparative assessment of ASF preparedness across countries and territories (hereafter "territories") in the Caribbean basin. The final sample size was 18 territories, 41% of the 44 territories identified as the target population in and around the Caribbean basin. Via semi-structured interviews, respondents completed a 0-10 agreement-scale questionnaire investigating ASF preparedness. Quantitative analysis was used to construct a territory-by-statement matrix and Spearman correlation matrix. Qualitative data were analyzed inductively. A wide range of preparedness scores were found, with the highest preparedness score observed for the presence of legislative authority to prevent and respond to ASF incursion, and the lowest score observed for the characterization of the feral swine population. papers.title: A unified YOLOv11 framework for multi-crop detection of diseases, pests and nutrient deficiencies, with preliminary field validation and mobile decision support
papers.authors: Hajar Hamdaoui, Hind Mesbah, Mashail Nasser Alzain, Yassine Zarrouk, Hanae Al Kaddouri
papers.abstract: Diseases, insect pests and nutrient deficiencies account for substantial annual crop losses worldwide, yet field diagnosis remains largely dependent on expert visual inspection. Although deep learning has shown considerable promise, most existing studies focus on a single crop or stress category under controlled conditions, with limited attention to nutrient deficiencies and few progressing to real-world deployment. This study presents a unified crop-stress detection framework covering 53 classes (41 biotic stresses, five nutrient deficiencies and seven healthy classes) across seven economically important crops of the Oriental region of Morocco. A dual-device dataset of 159,000 images was assembled, 90.4% acquired in the field with a DSLR camera and a smartphone and 9.6% from open-access sources used for training only. A lightweight YOLOv11n detector was trained at 832 × 832 resolution, with all settings selected on a separate field-acquired validation partition. Different types of activity, including industrial, constructional, heavy duty ones, etc., affect the health of workers during their activities. In this study, the Multi-Objective Decision-Making (MODM) method was combined with fuzzy TOPSIS to investigate and optimize the air pollution risk affecting the health and safety of construction workers of Lar City, Fars Province, Iran. Results: Accordingly, the results indicated that “understanding the risk” followed by “safety efficiency” affected the health risk of the construction workers the most. The samples were collected from 0 to 20 cm depth and measured using Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy (AAS) (PG990 Model). Results: The results showed that the mean concentrations of all toxic elements except arsenic had a higher value than the background values in the world. papers.title: Utilizing the invasive fruitwood Pyrus calleryana as substrate for mushroom cultivation, an experimental study in practical sustainability
papers.authors: Matthew D Helton
papers.source: OpenAlex / UTC Scholar (University of Tennessee at Chattanooga)
papers.abstract: This study evaluated the feasibility of using woodchips from the invasive Pyrus calleryana (Callery pear) as substrate for mushroom cultivation. Pleurotus ostreatus, Hericium erinaceus, and Ganoderma lucidum were grown on a pear wood substrate and on a conventional oak substrate to compare, yield, sensory attributes, and metabolite production. P. ostreatus showed no significant differences in yield or biological efficiency (p > 0.05), only sweetness (p = 0.022) differed significantly. H. erinaceus yield and efficiency were similar (p > 0.05), with greater second-flush yields in oak controls (p = 0.034) but no sensory differences (p > 0.05). G. lucidum performance was comparable across treatments (p > 0.05), yet triterpenoid content was reduced in pear substrates (p = 0.031). Results indicate P. calleryana biomass can sustain edible mushroom production without affecting yield or quality, while substrate composition influences bioactive metabolite synthesis, supporting invasive biomass valorization as a sustainable management strategy.

papers.title: Insect-resistant rice and Metarhizium anisopliae sustain the brown planthopper susceptibility through AMPK-mediated lipid redistribution
papers.authors: Kai Lin, Yutao Hu, Guy Smagghe, Wenqing Zhang
papers.abstract: The brown planthopper (BPH), Nilaparvata lugens, rapidly overcomes host resistance and develops insecticide resistance, undermining sustainable rice pest control. Here, we show that combining insect-resistant rice IR36 with the entomopathogenic fungus Metarhizium anisopliae CQMa421 provides durable suppression of BPH under laboratory conditions. Across multiple generations, chemical insecticides drove resistance and host adaptation, whereas M. anisopliae maintained susceptibility. Combined exposure redistributed lipids by reducing diacylglycerol (DAG) and adenosine triphosphate (ATP) in the fat body and ovary while increasing DAG in the hemolymph, thereby prioritizing humoral immunity. This redistribution was mediated by AMPK activation in the fat body, which inhibited insulin signaling and lipid catabolism while limiting detoxification and reproduction. AMPK-mediated energy reallocation sustained BPH sensitivity to both resistant rice and fungal infection. Integrating plant resistance with microbial biocontrol therefore suppresses host adaptation and delays resistance evolution, offering a sustainable pest management strategy.

Learning from COVID-19 to strengthen hantavirus preparedness and public health response
papers.authors: Salma Madihi, Warda Baha, Abdelouaheb Benani
papers.abstract: Years after the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic, the world continues to face significant health, social, and economic challenges, while emerging and re-emerging infectious diseases remain a growing global public health concern. This trend highlights the importance of interconnected health systems and reveals both the strengths and weaknesses of global public health preparedness and response. In this context, we present a comparative analysis of the COVID-19 pandemic and the recent Andes virus outbreak, focusing on their epidemiological and virological characteristics, and discussing the effectiveness of the COVID-19 public health responses. We also explore key lessons that can be applied to future zoonotic threats in the context of rapidly changing ecosystems. The results reveal that COVID-19 and hantavirus infections share several molecular and clinical features but differ in their transmission patterns. COVID-19 spreads efficiently between humans and caused a global pandemic, whereas Hantavirus infections are mainly transmitted from rodents to humans and remain geographically localized despite a higher case fatality rate. papers.title: Tomato Brown Rugose Fruit Virus and Pepino Mosaic Virus Differentially Modulate Disease Severity of Bacterial Pith Necrosis and Bacterial Canker in Tomato
papers.authors: Evanson Ngugi, Ilana Bekelman, Nir Berholz, Lior Avraham, Sigal Perets
papers.abstract: Worldwide tomato production is increasingly challenged by complex disease outbreaks involving multiple interacting pathogens. In Israel, recent years have seen a marked rise in vascular collapse symptoms in greenhouse-grown tomatoes, coinciding with the widespread emergence of tomato brown rugose fruit virus (ToBRFV) and pepino mosaic virus (PepMV). Here, we investigated the bacterial and viral agents associated with these outbreaks and examined how viral infection influences the development and severity of bacterial diseases that cause vascular collapse. Surveys conducted between 2021 and 2026 revealed that tomato pith necrosis outbreaks were associated with a diverse bacterial community dominated by members of the Pseudomonadales and Enterobacterales , while bacterial canker outbreaks were exclusively linked to Clavibacter michiganensis . papers.abstract: <jats:p>Background: Minimally invasive coronary artery bypass grafting (MICS CABG) via left anterior thoracotomy has emerged as a less invasive alternative to conventional open sternotomy (OPEN CABG), offering potential benefits in perioperative outcomes and complication rates. Objective. The aim of this study was to compare procedural characteristics, ventilation duration, drainage volumes, and postoperative complications between MICS CABG and OPEN CABG in a single-center cohort in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Methods. This retrospective cross-sectional study included 262 patients who underwent surgical revascularization between January 2019 and June 2023. Results. MICS CABG was associated with a shorter median procedure time (2.5 vs. 3.5 hours, p<0.001) and reduced mechanical ventilation duration (11.0 vs. 14.0 hours, p<0.001). Although ICU stay was similar (3.0 days, p=0.001), total hospitalization was shorter for MICS CABG (6.0 vs. 7.0 days, p<0.001). papers.abstract: Background: Working memory deficits, one of the earliest hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease (AD), are closely linked to abnormal neural activity in the dorsolateral prefrontal cortex (DLPFC). Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS), a non-invasive neuromodulation therapy, has been shown to ameliorate early AD working memory deficits by modulating excitatory activity in the DLPFC, yet the underlying mechanisms remain incompletely understood. Methods: This investigation was structured around 3 experimental phases. We initially applied tDCS to stimulate the left prefrontal cortex (PFC) of transgenic mice with 5 familial AD (5×FAD) 5 d per week for 4 weeks. Finally, we inhibited soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment receptor (SNARE) expression in the left PFC to elucidate the essential function of SNARE complex assembly with chaperone molecules in orchestrating synaptic vesicle release. papers.title: Predator-Induced Fear in a Modified RiceRatSnake Food Chain Model
papers.authors: Zakaria Zakaria, Dian Savitri
papers.source: OpenAlex / CAUCHY - Journal of Pure Mathematics and Applications (Universitas Islam Negeri Maulana Malik Ibrahim)
papers.abstract: Rice-field ecosystems involve trophic interactions among rice, herbivorous rats, and their natural predators, such as snakes. Beyond direct predation, predator presence can influence prey through non-consumptive fear effects that may alter population dynamics. This study develops and analyzes a modified riceratsnake food-chain model incorporating predator-induced fear into the effective ricerat interaction. The model is formulated as a system of three nonlinear ordinary differential equations and investigated through positivity and boundedness analyses, equilibrium analysis, local stability analysis using the Jacobian matrix and the RouthHurwitz criterion, and numerical simulations. The analytical results show that the solutions remain nonnegative and ultimately bounded, ensuring the biological feasibility of the model. Four equilibrium states are obtained: total extinction, rice-only persistence, ricerat coexistence, and full riceratsnake coexistence. papers.abstract: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a progressive neurodegenerative disease characterized by the selective degeneration of upper and lower motor neurons. One of the principal pathological hallmarks of ALS is the abnormal cytoplasmic mislocalization and aggregation of TAR DNA-binding protein 43 (TDP-43), a multifunctional RNA-binding protein involved in RNA metabolism and stress granule dynamics. Mutations in the TARDBP gene have been associated with both familial and sporadic ALS and are thought to contribute to altered cellular stress responses, defective RNA processing, and impaired proteostasis. The objective is to thoroughly study its distribution in the region and cabbage agrocenoses. In the Guba-Khachmaz economic region of Azerbaijan, the cabbage white butterfly (Pieris rapae) produces three complete generations. In the cabbage agrocenosis, first- and second-generation larvae of the pest cause the greatest damage to agricultural crops. The obtained results can be used in integrated pest control measures.

papers.authors: Guilherme Honório Fernández, Adriana Cavalieri Sais, Leonardo Pinto de Magalhães, Alexandre de Azevedo Olival
papers.abstract: Abstract Silvopastoral systems are vital for enhancing tropical pasture sustainability and mitigating degradation, yet their temporal dynamics under varying climates remain insufficiently quantified. This study evaluated the influence of tree cover on vegetation dynamics in an Amazonian silvopastoral system from 2016 to 2025. Sentinel-2 derived Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) and Normalized Difference Moisture Index (NDMI) time series were analyzed across 110 paddocks, utilizing Seasonal-Trend decomposition using LOESS to assess long-term trends and seasonal patterns. Tree cover percentage, extracted from Unmanned Aerial Vehicle imagery, was used to stratify paddocks. Results demonstrated that higher tree cover consistently correlated with elevated NDVI and NDMI values. During periods of lower precipitation (2019–2022), paddocks with greater tree cover exhibited slower declines and faster recoveries, indicating enhanced resistance to hydrological stress and reduced intra-annual variability. papers.abstract: Rice leaf disease is of important concern in developing countries, especially when the livelihood of a major population is dependent on agronomy. Rice is considered a staple crop in South Asian countries, foliar pathogens in rice cause substantial yield loss and economical burden. This review systematically examines the evolution of machine learning and state-of-the-art deep learning approaches for the detection of rice leaf disease. Unlike studies concentrated only on model performance, this review focused on the complete pipeline - spanning challenges observed during image acquisition, preprocessing steps, data characterization, features representation, classification methodology used, along with misused evaluation metrics leading to unsuccessful real-world deployment. This literature reveals a clear paradigm shift from handcrafted feature-based machine learning systems to deep learning architectures, because of their consistently high accuracy, learning discriminative representations directly from raw images without any human intervention. Methods: Six indoor/outdoor stations were established in three high-traffic districts of Tehran. Each station was sampled with six replicates in winter 2018 (36 samples in total). papers.title: One Health Approach to Combat Antibiotic Resistance: Human, Animal, and Environmental Health Integration for Sustainability in Solving Global Health Issues
papers.authors: Annual Methodological Archive Research Review
papers.source: OpenAlex / Annual Methodological Archive Research Review
papers.abstract: One of the key health challenges in the twenty-first century is antimicrobial resistance (AMR). Considering that I have gained extensive experience in human medicine, veterinary medicine and environmental health, it becomes evident that the problem of AMR cannot be truly grasped and managed if this challenge is viewed in the prism of any one sphere of human activity. Pathogens which gain antimicrobial resistance irrespective of substances used for their elimination are not bounded by man-made barriers of hospital wards, farms or rivers. For example, a strain of E. coli bacteria becoming resistant to the antibiotics in the chicken houses may occur in the surface water surrounding the farm in few weeks, then in the microbiome of the farm workers and finally – in the body of the patient suffering from urinary tract infection in a distant hospital (Woolhouse et al., 2015; Founou et al., 2016). This chapter will show that having taken into account the experience accumulated in more than two decades of research in the area of AMR policy and management, the One Health approach is not only a new trend, but the necessity.

papers.abstract: Landraces, especially of rye (Secale cereale L.), have emerged as viable crops for organic and small-scale farmers on marginal agricultural lands. This on-farm study investigates landrace rye cultivation by examining how environment, farmers’ management strategies and social context are related to overall performance of landrace rye. The study included 37 fields at 28 organic farms, seven different landraces of rye (of spring-, autumn- and midsummer-sown types): most of the farmers growing rye landraces in Sweden. Using interviews, participatory observation and sampling in the fields, we collected data on crop performance, soil data, landscape structure, and farmers’ management strategies and networks. Projections to Latent Structures analysis (PLS) was used to understand how management strategies and environment were related to rye performance. We found that farmers’ access to knowledge of landrace cereal cultivation through experience and networks was associated with better rye performance and with less winter damage (Variable of Importance in the Projection /VIP >1). This research was done to investigate the effect of drought stress, soil salinity, Piriformospora indica (P. indica), and MWCNs on biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil that contaminated with Pb and Cd under cultivation of triticale plant. Methods: Treatments consisted of applying MWCNs (2% [W/W]) in the Pb- and Cd-polluted soil that was simultaneously polluted with diesel oil (0, 5, and 10% [W/W]), and the plants used in this study were inoculated with P. indica. After 70 days, plants were harvested, and plant and soil Cd were measured using AAS (atomic absorption spectrometry). In addition, the degradation percentage of diesel oil in soil was determined. Results: Soil application of MWCNs at the rate of 2% (W/W) significantly increased the biodegradation of diesel oil in the soil in the drought and salinity (6 dS/m) stress by 11.3% and 15.6%, respectively. papers.authors: Rex Jeya Rajkumar Samdavid Thanapaul, Manoj Govindarajulu, Chetan Y. Pundkar, Peethambaran Arun
papers.abstract: Polytrauma with predominant musculoskeletal (MSK) injury, resulting from blast, blunt, and crush mechanisms, remains a leading and complex challenge in both military and civilian medicine. These injuries not only disrupt tissues structurally but also trigger systemic cascades involving immune imbalance, endothelial dysfunction, mitochondrial stress, and premature cellular senescence. Such pathological processes contribute to both immediate clinical instability and long-term complications such as fibrosis, aberrant bone formation, neuroinflammation, and chronic disability. Conventional injury assessments, which rely heavily on anatomical scoring and nonspecific blood markers, fail to capture the dynamic molecular landscape underlying these conditions. papers.abstract: Abstract Embryonic diapause and its termination are key to seasonal timing in the univoltine damselfly Lestes sponsa , ensuring that eggs overwinter and hatch in spring. Following summer oviposition—typically in plants above water—diapause begins after 2–3 weeks. We investigated diapause termination in eggs from southern Sweden (~ 55°N) using combinations of chilling in darkness and subsequent exposure to photoperiods at elevated temperatures. Diapause development—a physiological process underlying termination—was fastest at 10 °C, slower at 5 °C, and slowest (possibly stagnating) at 20–21 °C. Longer chilling enhanced the terminating effects of long photoperiods and high temperatures, resulting in faster, more synchronous hatching and a shorter critical photoperiod. At immediate 21 °C and solstice-like photoperiods (LD 19.5:4.5), hatching began 1–2 weeks after diapause initiation and continued for weeks, but synchrony improved with prior exposure to diapause-maintaining conditions (< LD 17:7). papers.abstract: Abstract Medicinal plants are valuable sources of phenolics, flavonoids, alkaloids, terpenoids, glycosides and essential oils. Phytochemicals extracted from medicinal plants find application in different biological systems due to their varied biological activities. Rising environmental concerns along with requirement for sustainable substitutes have gained interest in multifunctional compounds from plants. Plants possess phytochemicals with antioxidant, antimicrobial and corrosion inhibition potential which make them applicable in pharmaceutical industries, food processing, environmental and industrial applications. Antimicrobial activity is due to alteration of the microbial cell membrane structure, enzyme inhibition and binding with microbial DNA.
